subject: MSA / Order Form: proposed language for damages, exclusions, and examples
body:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA comments: damages and exclusions (first pass)

Soojin / Karthik —

Thanks for the draft MSA. A few quick items from our side on the limitation of liability and damage carve-outs:
- We want lost profits and diminution of business value to be recoverable in certain breach scenarios (e.g., persistent data corruption that directly causes measurable revenue loss).
- We need a clearer definition of "direct damages" vs "consequential/indirect".
- Carve-outs: for data loss (including forensic costs, reprocurement of lost data, and remediation fees) and for IP infringement we want narrower caps or no caps.

Can you propose example language that preserves your fee-based cap while giving us comfort on data loss and lost profits when Redwood materially breaches?

Appreciate it — happy to take a short call if easier.

— Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

---

On Sat, 1 Aug 2026 at 11:34 AM, soojin_lee@redwood.ai wrote:
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments: damages and exclusions (first pass)

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask. High-level our position is: (i) keep an aggregate cap tied to fees (12 months of fees or fees paid in the prior 12 months), and (ii) preserve standard carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, indemnification, and willful misconduct. We understand Acme's concern about business interruption and data loss — that is one of the most common negotiation points.

I looped in Neha (legal) and Laura (contracts) to propose concrete drafting alternatives and one compromise approach that we think is defensible from an operational and risk perspective. We'll propose both a conservative and a customer-friendly option so you can see the trade-offs.

Propose a 30-minute call Monday to walk through examples — our calendar is flexible.

Best,
Soojin
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

---

On Sun, 2 Aug 2026 at 09:05 AM, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-analytics.com>, Bethany King <bethany.king@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft redlines and explanatory examples (direct vs indirect)

Alex / team —

Below are three drafting approaches: (A) Redwood baseline (conservative), (B) Compromise (commercially reasonable middle ground), and (C) Customer-friendly (broader carve-outs). After each block I include short examples to illustrate what would be recoverable under the language.

A. Redwood baseline (recommended for risk):
- Limitation of Liability: "Except to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or Redwood's breach of its confidentiality obligations or indemnity obligations, the aggregate liability of Redwood and its affiliates for any and all claims arising out of or relating to the Agreement shall not exceed the aggregate amounts paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months prior to the event giving rise to the claim."
- Exclusions: "In no event shall either party be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of revenue, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of goodwill."

Illustrative outcome (baseline): Lost profits resulting from unavailability are excluded unless they fall within an indemnity or gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out. Data restoration costs would be excluded as consequential unless Redwood's breach also constitutes willful misconduct or a specific indemnity applies.

B. Compromise (recommended as starting point):
- Limitation of Liability: "Except as set forth below, the aggregate liability of Redwood shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months prior to the claim, or (ii) $500,000."
- Carve-outs to cap: 
  - Notwithstanding the foregoing, the liability cap shall not apply to (i) Redwood's indemnity obligations for third party IP infringement; (ii) damages arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; and (iii) documented direct costs to repair or restore Customer data that are incurred as a direct result of Redwood's breach, provided such costs are reasonable, documented, and pre-approved (except in emergencies).
- Definition examples: "Direct damages" means documented, out-of-pocket costs directly incurred to remedy the breach (e.g., reasonable costs to restore lost customer data from backups, documented third-party forensic fees). "Indirect damages" includes lost profits, loss of business, loss of goodwill, and other incidental consequential losses.

Illustrative outcome (compromise): If Redwood's defect caused database corruption and Customer paid a third party $120,000 to recover data, those documented recovery costs would qualify as direct damages (carved out of the cap). However, Acme's claim for lost sales due to downtime would remain excluded as indirect/consequential.

C. Customer-friendly (more favorable to Acme):
- Limitation of Liability: "Except as set forth below, the aggregate liability of Redwood shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer in the prior twelve (12) months, or (ii) $2,000,000."
- Carve-outs: No cap for (i) IP infringement indemnity, (ii) breach of confidentiality leading to unauthorized disclosure of Customer data, (iii) direct damages for data loss and remediation, and (iv) proven lost profits resulting directly from Redwood's material breach.

Illustrative outcome (customer-friendly): Acme could recover both documented data restoration costs and measurable lost profits if they can tie the revenue loss directly to Redwood's material breach.

Operational & evidentiary suggestions:
- For data-related claims, require (i) contemporaneous logging and incident reports; (ii) third-party forensic invoices or remediation receipts; and (iii) a reasonable pre-approval process for remediation vendors where practicable. This reduces disputes over "reasonableness."
- For lost profits, limit recoverable amounts to demonstrable, documented revenue loss (e.g., contract cancellations with signed notices) rather than speculative projections.

Drafting examples to consider inserting into the MSA (short snippets):
1) Definition: "Direct Damages" means reasonable, documented, out-of-pocket costs actually incurred by Customer to repair, replace or restore lost or corrupted Customer data and to remediate security incidents, but expressly excludes lost profits, loss of business, or other indirect or consequential damages.

2) Direct-cost carve-out: "Notwithstanding any limitation or exclusion of liability in this Agreement, Redwood's liability for direct costs to repair or restore Customer data shall not be limited to the cap, provided such costs are reasonable, documented, and necessarily incurred as a direct result of Redwood's breach."

3) Consequential exclusion (sample): "Except for liability arising from Redwood's willful misconduct, gross negligence, or indemnity obligations, neither party shall be liable for consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including but not limited to lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of goodwill."

Happy to put these redlines into the Word document. If we take approach B, operationally we'll need to agree a simple pre-approval path for data restoration vendors and a template form for forensic invoices to avoid back-and-forth.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

On Sun, 2 Aug 2026 at 12:18 PM, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-analytics.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments: damages and exclusions (first pass)

Alex —

Thanks for the context. If your team is okay with approach B we'll mark the Word doc accordingly and include a short operational addendum for pre-approvals (one-paragraph). That approach keeps our exposure bounded while giving Acme a realistic path to recover documented data remediation costs.

Can we confirm whether Acme expects any specific minimums for documentation (e.g., do you need signed statements from forensics vendors or just invoices)? Happy to accept an example template you use.

Karthik
VP, Sales, Redwood Inference

---

On Sun, 2 Aug 2026 at 16:05:00 -07:00, Bethany King <bethany.king@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments: damages and exclusions (first pass)

Team —

Appreciate the options. Acme's procurement preference is approach B with the following clarifications: (1) data restoration carve-out should explicitly include reasonable third-party forensic costs and costs to re-ingest/transmit historical data from backups; (2) lost profits remain excluded unless Acme can provide signed customer cancellation notices or direct, contemporaneous revenue evidence; and (3) pre-approval for vendors should be possible post-incident if the incident timeline makes pre-approval impractical.

We'll review the markup you prepare and aim to get back with a final pass by EOD Tuesday. Also attaching our standard forensic vendor form for your reference (see attachment stub: ACME_Forensic-Vendor-Form.pdf).

Thanks,
Bethany King
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

---

Next steps agreed: Redwood to produce redline file with approach B language, include one-paragraph operations addendum for post-incident vendor approval, and insert the two short definition snippets above. Proposed internal owners: Neha to draft, Laura to perform final contract review, Soojin/Karthik to present to Acme.

Attachments referenced in thread: ACME_MSA_marked_v3.docx (markup), Redwood-damage-examples.pdf (internal note), ACME_Forensic-Vendor-Form.pdf (external form).
